191	static leResult setPressed(leButtonWidget* _this,
192	                           leBool pressed)
193	{
194	    leBool dirty = LE_FALSE;
195	
196	    LE_ASSERT_THIS();
197	    
198	    if(pressed == LE_TRUE && _this->state == LE_BUTTON_STATE_TOGGLED)
199	        return LE_FAILURE;
200	        
201	    if(pressed == LE_TRUE)
202	    {
203	        if(_this->pressedEvent != NULL)
204	        {
205	            _this->pressedEvent(_this);
206	        }
207	            
208	        // move to toggled state
209	        if(_this->toggleable == LE_TRUE)
210	        {
211	            _this->state = LE_BUTTON_STATE_TOGGLED;
212	        }
213	        // throw released event immediately
214	        else
215	        {
216	            if(_this->releasedEvent != NULL)
217	            {
218	                _this->releasedEvent(_this);
219	            }
220	        }
221	    }
222	    else
223	    {
224	        _this->state = LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP;
225	        
226	        if(_this->releasedEvent != NULL)
227	        {
228	            _this->releasedEvent(_this);
229	        }
230	    }
231	    
232	    // try to find a reason to redraw
233	    if(_this->pressedImage != NULL && 
234	       _this->pressedImage != _this->releasedImage)
235	    {
236	        dirty = LE_TRUE;
237	    }
238	       
239	    if(_this->widget.style.borderType == LE_WIDGET_BORDER_BEVEL)
240	    {
241	        dirty = LE_TRUE;
242	    }
243	        
244	    if(_this->pressedOffset != 0 &&
245	       (_this->pressedImage != NULL ||
246	       (_this->string != NULL && _this->string->fn->isEmpty(_this->string) == LE_FALSE)))
247	    {
248	        dirty = LE_TRUE;
249	    }
250	        
251	    if(dirty == LE_TRUE)
252	    {
253	        _this->fn->invalidate(_this);
254	    }
255	
256	#if LE_DEBUG == 1
257	    _leDebugNotify_WidgetPropertyChanged((leWidget*)_this);
258	#endif
259	
260	    return LE_SUCCESS;
261	}

505	static void touchDown(leButtonWidget* _this,
506	                      leWidgetEvent_TouchDown* evt)
507	{
508	    LE_ASSERT_THIS();
509	
510	    leWidgetEvent_Accept((leWidgetEvent*)evt, (leWidget*)_this);
511	
512	    if(_this->toggleable == LE_TRUE)
513	    {
514	        if(_this->state != LE_BUTTON_STATE_TOGGLED)
515	        {
516	            _this->state = LE_BUTTON_STATE_DOWN;

519	            {
520	                _this->pressedEvent(_this);

522	        }
523	    }
524	    else
525	    {
526	        _this->state = LE_BUTTON_STATE_DOWN;
527	
528	        if(_this->pressedEvent != NULL)
529	        {
530	            _this->pressedEvent(_this);
531	        }
532	    }
533	
534	    if (_this->pressedOffset != 0 || 
535	        (_this->pressedImage != _this->releasedImage) ||
536	        (_this->widget.style.backgroundType != LE_WIDGET_BACKGROUND_NONE) || 
537	        (_this->widget.style.borderType != LE_WIDGET_BORDER_NONE))
538	    {
539	        _this->fn->invalidate(_this);
540	    }
541	
542	    //printf("button touch down\n");

545	static void touchUp(leButtonWidget* _this,
546	                    leWidgetEvent_TouchUp* evt)
547	{
548	    leRect rect;
549	    lePoint pnt;
550	    
551	    LE_ASSERT_THIS();
552	    
553	    _this->fn->localRect(_this, &rect);
554	
555	    pnt.x = evt->x;
556	    pnt.y = evt->y;
557	
558	    leWidgetEvent_Accept((leWidgetEvent*)evt, (leWidget*)_this);
559	
560	    leUtils_ClipRectToParent(_this->widget.parent, &rect);
561	    leUtils_RectToScreenSpace((leWidget*)_this, &rect);
562	    
563	    //Toggle buttons will not respond to touch outside the button area
564	    if ((leRectContainsPoint(&rect, &pnt) == LE_FALSE) && 
565	        (_this->toggleable == LE_TRUE))
566	    {
567	        return;
568	    }
569	
570	    if(leRectContainsPoint(&rect, &pnt) == LE_TRUE)
571	    {
572	        if(_this->toggleable == LE_TRUE)
573	        {
574	            if(_this->state == LE_BUTTON_STATE_TOGGLED)
575	            {
576	                _this->state = LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP;
577	
578	                if(_this->releasedEvent != NULL)
579	                {
580	                    _this->releasedEvent(_this);
581	                }
582	                
583	                //printf("_this released\n");
584	            }
585	            else
586	            {
587	                _this->state = LE_BUTTON_STATE_TOGGLED;
588	            }
589	        }
590	        else
591	        {
592	            _this->state = LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP;
593	
594	            if(_this->releasedEvent != NULL)
595	            {
596	                _this->releasedEvent(_this);
597	            }
598	            
599	            //printf("_this released\n");
600	        }
601	    }
602	    else
603	    {
604	        if(_this->toggleable == LE_TRUE)
605	        {
606	            if(_this->state != LE_BUTTON_STATE_TOGGLED)
607	            {
608	                _this->state = LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP;
609	            }
610	        }
611	        else
612	        {
613	            _this->state = LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP;
614	        }
615	    }
616	    
617	    if (_this->pressedOffset != 0 || 
618	        (_this->pressedImage != _this->releasedImage) ||
619	        (_this->widget.style.backgroundType != LE_WIDGET_BACKGROUND_NONE) || 
620	        (_this->widget.style.borderType != LE_WIDGET_BORDER_NONE))
621	    {
622	        _this->fn->invalidate(_this);
623	    }
624	
625	    //printf("button touch up\n");
626	}

97	            imgRect->height = btn->releasedImage->buffer.size.height;
98	        }
99	    }
100

102	    
103	    leUtils_ArrangeRectangle(imgRect,

123	    // move the rect to screen space

194	void _leButtonWidget_InvalidateBorderAreas(const leButtonWidget* btn)
195	{
196	    leRect rect, dmgRect;
197		int32_t left, top, right, bottom;
198		
199		if(btn->widget.style.borderType == LE_WIDGET_BORDER_NONE)
200		    return;
201		
202		btn->fn->rectToScreen(btn, &rect);
203		
204		if(btn->widget.style.borderType == LE_WIDGET_BORDER_LINE)
205		{
206		    if(rect.width == 0 || rect.height == 0)
207				return;
208	
209			if(rect.width <= 1 || rect.height <= 1)
210			{
211			    btn->fn->_damageArea(btn, &rect);
212	
213				return;
214			}
215		
216		    left = 1;
217		    top = 1;
218		    right = 1;
219		    bottom = 1;
220		}
221		else
222		{
223		    if(rect.width == 0 || rect.height == 0)
224				return;
225	
226			if(rect.width <= 3 || rect.height <= 3)
227			{
228			    btn->fn->_damageArea(btn, &rect);
229				
230				return;
231	        }
232	        
233	        right = 2;
234	        bottom = 2;
235	        
236	        if(btn->state == LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP)
237	        {
238	            left = 1;
239	            top = 1;
240	        }
241	        else
242	        {
243	            left = 2;
244		        top = 2;
245		    }
246		}
247		
248		// left line
249		dmgRect.x = rect.x;
250		dmgRect.y = rect.y;
251		dmgRect.width = left;
252		dmgRect.height = rect.height;
253	
254		btn->fn->_damageArea(btn, &dmgRect);
255	
256		// top line
257		dmgRect.width = rect.width;
258		dmgRect.height = top;
259	
260		btn->fn->_damageArea(btn, &dmgRect);
261	
262		// right line
263		dmgRect.x = rect.x + rect.width - right;
264		dmgRect.y = rect.y;
265		dmgRect.width = right;
266		dmgRect.height = rect.height;
267	
268		btn->fn->_damageArea(btn, &dmgRect);
269	
270		// bottom line
271		dmgRect.x = rect.x;
272		dmgRect.y = rect.y + rect.height - bottom;
273		dmgRect.width = rect.width;
274		dmgRect.height = bottom;
275	
276		btn->fn->_damageArea(btn, &dmgRect);
277	}

282	static void drawBorder(leButtonWidget* btn);
283	static void nextState(leButtonWidget* btn)
284	{
285	    switch(btn->widget.status.drawState)
286	    {
287	        case NOT_STARTED:
288	        {
289	            paintState.alpha = 255;
290	
291	#if LE_ALPHA_BLENDING_ENABLED == 1
292	            if(btn->fn->getCumulativeAlphaEnabled(btn) == LE_TRUE)
293	            {
294	                paintState.alpha = btn->fn->getCumulativeAlphaAmount(btn);
295	            }
296	#endif
297	            
298	            if(btn->widget.style.backgroundType != LE_WIDGET_BACKGROUND_NONE)
299	            {
300	                btn->widget.status.drawState = DRAW_BACKGROUND;
301	                btn->widget.drawFunc = (leWidget_DrawFunction_FnPtr)&drawBackground;
302	
303	                return;
304	            }
305	        }
306	        // fall through
307	        case DRAW_BACKGROUND:
308	        {
309	            if((btn->state != LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP && btn->pressedImage != NULL) ||
310	               (btn->state == LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP && btn->releasedImage != NULL))
311	            {
312	                btn->widget.status.drawState = DRAW_IMAGE;
313	                btn->widget.drawFunc = (leWidget_DrawFunction_FnPtr)&drawImage;
314	
315	                return;
316	            }
317	        }
318	        // fall through
319	        case DRAW_IMAGE:
320	        {            
321	            if(btn->string != NULL && btn->string->fn->isEmpty(btn->string) == LE_FALSE)
322	            {
323	                btn->widget.status.drawState = DRAW_STRING;
324	                btn->widget.drawFunc = (leWidget_DrawFunction_FnPtr)&drawString;
325	
326	                return;
327	            }
328	        }
329	        // fall through
330	        case DRAW_STRING:
331	        {
332	            if(btn->widget.style.borderType != LE_WIDGET_BORDER_NONE)
333	            {
334	                btn->widget.drawFunc = (leWidget_DrawFunction_FnPtr)&drawBorder;
335	                btn->widget.status.drawState = DRAW_BORDER;
336	                
337	                return;
338	            }
339	        }
340	        // fall through
341	        case DRAW_BORDER:
342	        {
343	            btn->widget.status.drawState = DONE;
344	            btn->widget.drawFunc = NULL;
345	        }
346	    }
347	}

350	{
351	    if(btn->widget.style.backgroundType == LE_WIDGET_BACKGROUND_FILL)
352	    {
353	        if(btn->state != LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP)
354	        {
355	            leWidget_SkinClassic_DrawBackground((leWidget*)btn,
356	                                                leScheme_GetRenderColor(btn->widget.scheme, LE_SCHM_BACKGROUND),
357	                                                paintState.alpha);
358	        }
359	        else
360	        {
361	            leWidget_SkinClassic_DrawBackground((leWidget*)btn,
362	                                                leScheme_GetRenderColor(btn->widget.scheme, LE_SCHM_BASE),
363	                                                paintState.alpha);
364	        }
365	    }
366	
367	    nextState(btn);
368	}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-19 18:33:43Z)**_

I've got the full picture now. Here's the answer.

## What the stock button gives you already

Two things you're asking for are already supported without any custom code:

**Rounded corners** — the base widget has `cornerRadius` ([legato_widget_button.c:786-787](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/button/legato_widget_button.c#L786-L787) wires `getCornerRadius`/`setCornerRadius`). The button's background draw routes through [`leWidget_SkinClassic_DrawBackground`](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/legato_widget_skin_classic_common.c#L296), which honors `cornerRadius`:

```c
if (style.cornerRadius > 0 &&
    (borderType == LE_WIDGET_BORDER_NONE || borderType == LE_WIDGET_BORDER_LINE))
    FillRoundCornerRect(...)
```

⚠️ Caveat: rounded corners are **only** drawn when `borderType` is `NONE` or `LINE`. The button constructor defaults to `LE_WIDGET_BORDER_BEVEL` ([button.c:119](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/button/legato_widget_button.c#L119)), which gives square beveled edges. So: `setBorderType(LE_WIDGET_BORDER_LINE)` (or `NONE`) + `setCornerRadius(n)` and the stock button rounds itself.

**Color** — every color in the skin (`drawBackground`, `drawString`, `drawBorder`) comes from `leScheme_GetRenderColor(btn->widget.scheme, LE_SCHM_*)`. There is no per-widget color field; the skin always reads the scheme. So the supported way to "set color" is to give the widget its **own `leScheme` instance** and set `base`/`background`/`text`/`shadowDark` to what you want, then `setScheme()`. That's a scheme, but it's a private one you control at runtime — no MHGC scheme editing.

## Can you override the draw functions?

`LE_DYNAMIC_VTABLES == 0` ([legato_config.h:63](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/legato_config.h#L63)), so `buttonWidgetVTable` is a `const static` table shared by *all* button instances. You can't patch it in place. But the widget's `fn` pointer is a per-instance `void*`, and the library deliberately exposes `_leButtonWidget_FillVTable()` to copy the table. That gives you three real options:

**Option A — per-instance custom vtable (lightest, no lib edits).** Copy the button vtable into a RAM struct, override `_paint`, and point your instance at it:

```c
static leButtonWidgetVTable myVT;   // RAM copy
_leButtonWidget_FillVTable(&myVT);  // clone stock behavior
myVT._paint = myButton_Paint;       // your paint routine

// after constructing the button:
btn->widget.fn = &myVT;
btn->fn        = &myVT;
```

In `myButton_Paint` you call the `leWidget_SkinClassic_*` helpers (they're all exported, non-static) or raw `leRenderer_*` primitives with **literal colors** — e.g. `leWidget_SkinClassic_FillRoundCornerRect(&rect, myColor, radius, alpha)` — fully bypassing the scheme. This is the cleanest way to get *both* arbitrary color and rounded corners with bevel, without touching the generated library.

**Option B — full custom widget subclass.** Make a new type that constructs a `leWidget` base, supplies its own vtable + paint state machine. More boilerplate; only worth it if you need new behavior/state beyond a button, since you'd reimplement touch handling etc.

**Option C — edit the generated skin** ([legato_widget_button_skin_classic.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/button/legato_widget_button_skin_classic.c)). Don't — it lives under `config/default/` and MHGC will regenerate over it.

## Recommendation

- If "rounded + a different color" is all you need → **no custom drawing**: `borderType = LINE/NONE`, `setCornerRadius`, and give the button a private `leScheme`. Zero risk, survives regeneration.
- If you need rounded corners *with the bevel look*, or true scheme-independent coloring, or a gradient/etc → **Option A** (per-instance vtable with a custom `_paint`). It's contained, doesn't fight MHGC, and reuses the existing skin helpers.

Want me to sketch the Option A `_paint` for the exact look you're after (rounded, filled with a fixed color, with text)? If so, tell me: bevel or flat, and whether the text/pressed-offset behavior should stay as-is. This is marvin UI work — if we go with a custom paint I'll note the decision in [firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md](firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md).

#include "gfx/legato/generated/le_gen_init.h"

static int32_t currentScreen;
static int32_t changingToScreen;

void legato_initializeScreenState(void)
{
    leSetStringTable(&stringTable);

    initializeStrings();

    screenInit_Screen0();

    currentScreen = -1;
    changingToScreen = -1;

    legato_showScreen(screenID_Screen0);
}

uint32_t legato_getCurrentScreen(void)
{
    return currentScreen;
}

static void legato_hideCurrentScreen(void)
{
    switch(currentScreen)
    {
        case screenID_Screen0:
        {
            screenHide_Screen0();
            currentScreen = 0;
            break;
        }
    }
}

void legato_showScreen(uint32_t id)
{
    if(changingToScreen >= 0)
        return;

    changingToScreen = id;
}

void legato_updateScreenState(void)
{
    if(leIsDrawing() == LE_TRUE)
        return;

    if(changingToScreen >= 0)
    {
        legato_hideCurrentScreen();

        leEvent_ClearList();

        switch(changingToScreen)
        {
            case screenID_Screen0:
            {
                screenShow_Screen0();
                break;
            }
        }

        currentScreen = changingToScreen;
        changingToScreen = -1;
    }

    switch(currentScreen)
    {
        case screenID_Screen0:
        {
            screenUpdate_Screen0();
            break;
        }
    }
}

leBool legato_isChangingScreens(void)
{
    return changingToScreen != -1;
}

Confirmed everything I need. Here's the situation and the clean path.

## Why this is actually easy in your case

Two pieces of good news from the code:

1. **The buttons are already `LE_WIDGET_BORDER_LINE`** ([le_gen_screen_Screen0.c:60](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/generated/screen/le_gen_screen_Screen0.c#L60), etc.). Corner radius is only honored for `NONE`/`LINE` borders ([legato_widget.c:1316-1318](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/legato_widget.c#L1316-L1318)) — so you're already in the supported regime. No border-type change needed.
2. **`setCornerRadius` self-invalidates** ([legato_widget.c:1325](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/legato_widget.c#L1325)) — so you can apply it any time after the screen is up and it repaints itself. No manual invalidate.
3. The widget pointers (`Screen0_Button_Manual_*`) are **exported globals** in the generated header, so app code can reach them directly.

So all you need is to call `setCornerRadius(btn, n)` on each button *after* `screenShow_Screen0()` has created them. No draw override, no custom widget, no scheme work.

## The one catch: timing

`screenShow_Screen0()` runs lazily inside the generated `_LEGATO_Tasks` loop ([tasks.c:119](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/tasks.c#L119)), not at init — the globals are NULL until then, and they're recreated on every hide/show. So the override has to fire *after* show, and you don't want to edit generated code.

## Recommended approach — app-owned, regeneration-proof

You already have [ui/manual_input.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/../../ui/manual_input.c) as the glue file that owns these buttons. Put the styling there:

```c
/* ui/manual_input.c */
#define MANUAL_BTN_CORNER_RADIUS 12

void ManualInput_StyleButtons(void)
{
    leButtonWidget* btns[] = {
        Screen0_Button_Manual_Green, Screen0_Button_Manual_Red,
        Screen0_Button_Manual_Yellow, Screen0_Button_Manual_Blue,
        Screen0_Button_Manual_Orange, Screen0_Button_Manual_StrumDown,
        Screen0_Button_Manual_StrumUp, Screen0_Button_Manual_Enable,
    };
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof(btns)/sizeof(btns[0]); i++)
        btns[i]->fn->setCornerRadius(btns[i], MANUAL_BTN_CORNER_RADIUS);
}
```

Then trigger it once after the screen exists. Cleanest no-generated-edit trigger, given the only GUI loop is generated: a **one-shot latch** that runs from one of marvin's existing app-owned task loops (or a tiny dedicated task spawned in `APP_Initialize`):

```c
static bool styled = false;
if (!styled && Screen0_Button_Manual_Green != NULL) {
    ManualInput_StyleButtons();
    styled = true;
}
```

(If you ever hide/show the screen, re-arm `styled = false` when the pointer goes NULL.)

## Alternative — MHGC "Screen Show" event

Composer can emit a per-screen show callback: enable the Screen0 *Show* event, and it regenerates `screenShow_Screen0()` to call a handler you implement in app code (e.g. `ManualInput_StyleButtons()` from `ui/manual_input.c`). This is the most Legato-idiomatic trigger and removes the latch — the tradeoff is it regenerates the screen file (expected; you still never hand-edit it). Corner radius itself still isn't exposed, so the body stays in your code either way.

## My recommendation

Go with the **one-shot latch calling `ManualInput_StyleButtons()`** — it's entirely in app-owned files, survives regeneration with zero MHGC fiddling, and reuses the file that already owns these widgets. Tell me which existing marvin task loop is the right home for the latch (or if you'd prefer the tiny dedicated task), and I'll wire it up and note the decision in [firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md](firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md).

One question on intent: do you also want a non-scheme **color** override on these, or just the rounded corners for now? The buttons currently pull color from per-color schemes (`GreenScheme`, etc.), which already works — corner radius was the only gap.
